channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Cotton Yields Reach 80-90 Centners Per Hectare in Samarkand
item.description: Cotton yields of 80-90 centners per hectare are being achieved in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, thanks to the 'Xinjiang' agrotechnology. This innovative practice was tested on a farm in Kattakorgan district, resulting in reduced costs and increased yields compared to previous years.

item.title: Inmates Injure Themselves in Atyrau Pre-trial Detention Center
item.description: Inmates at the Atyrau pre-trial detention center injured themselves on October 23, demanding relocation from a quarantine block. They protested sanitary conditions, sewage issues, poor food, and restrictions on permitted items. The regional penal system department confirmed the incident, stating five individuals accused of serious crimes were involved. A criminal case for group disobedience has been initiated.

item.title: Taliban Fighters Wounded in Clashes in Afghanistan's Badghis Province
item.description: Several Taliban fighters were reportedly wounded in attacks on their checkpoints in the Tagab Alam, Jawand, and Qadis districts of Badghis province. Clashes have occurred over recent nights. In a separate incident, a Taliban member escaped custody, killed another fighter, and fled. These events follow an increase in clashes between the Taliban and opposition fronts.

item.title: Global Leaders Congratulate Kazakhstan on Republic Day
item.description: Leaders from around the world, including presidents Putin, Xi Jinping, and Donald Trump, have sent congratulatory messages to Kazakhstan on Republic Day. The messages acknowledged Kazakhstan's development, political reforms, economic progress, and expressed intentions to strengthen bilateral cooperation. President Tokayev received the greetings.

item.title: Group Protest by Prisoners Occurs in Atyrau Pre-trial Detention Center
item.description: A group protest by prisoners has taken place in the pre-trial detention center in Atyrau. Further details regarding the cause or scale of the protest were not immediately available.

item.title: World Leaders Congratulate Kazakhstan on Republic Day
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has received congratulatory messages from heads of foreign states and international organizations on the occasion of Kazakhstan's Republic Day. Leaders from Russia and China highlighted Kazakhstan's political reforms, economic development, and international standing in their messages.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Attends Republic Day Flag Raising Ceremony in Astana
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev participated in a solemn flag-raising ceremony in Astana to mark Republic Day. The event took place on the square in front of the Akorda residence. The national flag was raised, accompanied by the national anthem. Similar ceremonies are scheduled across all regions of the country.

item.title: Ten-Tek Mine Exceeds One Million Tons of Coal Production for First Time in a Decade
item.description: The 'Ten-Tek' mine, part of Qarmet company, has reached a significant milestone, producing over one million tons of coal for the first time in ten years. Production is planned to increase to 1.2 million tons by the end of 2026. The mine is undergoing modernization, including new ventilation shafts and equipment.

item.title: Elon Musk Claims Ukraine Misused Starlink for Attacks, Citing Terms of Service Violation
item.description: Elon Musk stated that SpaceX's Starlink service was misused by Ukraine for offensive attacks, violating terms of service. He clarified that Starlink is intended for civilian use, not military attacks, and that a military-grade system, Starshield, is under US government control. Musk mentioned that the issue causing the misuse was resolved last week, but its impact on Starlink's performance in Ukraine remains unclear.

item.title: Barack Obama Criticizes Trump's Iran Policy, Citing Economic and Strategic Consequences
item.description: Former U.S. President Barack Obama criticized President Donald Trump's policy towards Iran, stating it has driven up global prices for goods and allowed Iran to gain control over the Strait of Hormuz. Obama highlighted his administration's diplomatic achievement in preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon through the 2015 JCPOA agreement, contrasting it with Trump's approach.

item.title: Hemodialysis Center to Open in Kerben Following Sewerage System Upgrade
item.description: A hemodialysis center is planned to open in Kerben, Kyrgyzstan, after the completion of a new sewerage system. President Sadyr Japarov confirmed the plan during a meeting with residents. The center aims to address patient travel difficulties for dialysis treatment. Currently, 56 residents of the Aksy district receive dialysis.

item.title: Afghanistan and Turkmenistan Discuss Expansion of Herat Gas Pipeline
item.description: Afghanistan and Turkmenistan are discussing the expansion and distribution networks of the Herat gas pipeline. During a visit, the Afghan Gas chief also met with international companies to explore opportunities for technical and commercial cooperation related to the project.

item.title: UN Supports Afghan Returnee Women in Establishing and Expanding Businesses
item.description: The UN Development Programme in Afghanistan is helping women returning from Iran launch and grow businesses, creating income and jobs. In Kunduz province, women entrepreneurs received financial aid, equipment, and training, enabling a dairy business to produce 400-500 kg of yogurt daily and employ 12 people, including seven returnees. This initiative is funded by Japan.

item.title: Uzbek President congratulates Interior Ministry staff on 35th anniversary
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated Interior Ministry staff and veterans on the 35th anniversary of the ministry's establishment. He emphasized their dedication to ensuring public safety and protecting citizens' rights and interests, noting their crucial role in maintaining peace and security across the country.

item.title: Afghan official: 1,119 civilians killed or injured in Pakistani attacks since 2022
item.description: Abdul Qahar Balkhi, spokesperson for Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated that 1,119 Afghan civilians have been killed or injured in Pakistani military attacks since the beginning of 2022. He reported that women and children constituted the majority of casualties and cited a Pakistani strike on a Kabul treatment center that allegedly killed hundreds.

item.title: Kyrgyz President urges mining firms to protect nature and restore land
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov reminded mining companies of their responsibility to protect nature and adhere to environmental requirements. He stressed the importance of full technical and biological land reclamation after resource extraction to avoid harming the environment for future generations. The president also highlighted infrastructure development, including road construction.

item.title: Inmates riot at Atyrau pre-trial detention center, several injured
item.description: Inmates at the Atyrau pre-trial detention center staged a protest against detention conditions, resulting in self-inflicted injuries. The Committee of the Criminal-Executive System reported that five inmates involved in the incident have been charged with organizing group disobedience. The situation is currently stable.

item.title: Economist analyzes Kazakhstan's economic growth and per capita GDP figures
item.description: Political analyst Andrey Chebotarev has analyzed Kazakhstan's development indicators, noting a 30% economic growth since 2019, averaging 4.5% annually. Per capita GDP has surpassed $15,000 nominally, with purchasing power parity around $35-40,000. Life expectancy is nearing 76 years, the highest in the region.

item.title: Kyrgyz President orders incubators for premature newborns in two cities
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has instructed officials to procure incubators for premature newborns in the cities of Tash-Kumyr and Kara-Kul. The request came from local residents during the president's visit to the Jalal-Abad region. The Ministry of Health confirmed the feasibility of acquiring the equipment.

item.title: President Participates in State Flag Raising Ceremony in Astana
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev attended the state flag raising ceremony in Astana, marking Republic Day. The event took place in front of the Akorda residence, featuring the national anthem and the raising of the flag. Similar ceremonies are scheduled across all regions of Kazakhstan.

item.title: Afghan Interior Minister Urges National Unity and Improved Security Force Conduct
item.description: Sirajuddin Haqqani called for stronger national unity, better relations between citizens and security forces, and increased public awareness to end rivalries. He emphasized that maintaining security is a shared responsibility and urged religious scholars and elders to promote reconciliation. Haqqani also instructed security officials to serve the public respectfully and expressed optimism about Afghanistan's progress.

item.title: Passenger Train Collides with Truck in Kazakhstan's Karaganda Region
item.description: A passenger train and a truck collided at an unregulated railway crossing in the Shet district of Kazakhstan's Karaganda region. The truck driver reportedly failed to ensure the safety of passage, but no injuries were reported.

item.title: Israel Restricts Palestinian Workers' Entry to West Bank Ahead of Elections
item.description: The Israeli military announced that Palestinian workers with permits will be barred from entering Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank on Sunday and Monday. Restrictions also apply to industrial zones. On election day, all entry and exit from the West Bank and Jordan Valley will be blocked, with land crossings closed. Settlers have also reportedly prevented farmers from harvesting olives.

item.title: Kazakhstan Hosts Media Forum on Oil and Gas Industry Coverage
item.description: A national media forum, Media Energy Talks, was held in Astana to discuss the coverage of the oil and gas sector. The event, attended by the Deputy Minister of Energy, explored how to report on complex technological and economic processes, and the impact of AI and social media on journalism. Masterclasses on oilfield services and fuel markets were also conducted.

item.title: Over 400,000 Protest Across France Against Cost of Living and Nationalism
item.description: At least 410,000 people participated in protests across France on October 24, according to the Interior Ministry. Unions reported up to 800,000 attendees. Protesters voiced anger over inflation, high fuel prices, poor public services, and wealth inequality. Clashes with police occurred in several cities, including Paris, leading to arrests.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy Shows Strong Growth, Exceeding Regional Averages
item.description: Kazakhstan's economy has grown by approximately 30% since 2019, averaging about 4.5% annually, a respectable pace for a developing nation. GDP per capita has surpassed $15,000 nominally, with purchasing power parity estimates around $35-40,000. Life expectancy has reached nearly 76 years, the best in the region. The country has advanced its automotive and rail industries from minimal localization to full-cycle production.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Suspected of Assaulting Taxi Driver in South Korea
item.description: An Uzbek citizen is suspected of assaulting a taxi driver in Hwaseong city, South Korea. The suspect allegedly attacked the driver who was attempting to film his illegal taxi service. The 50-year-old Korean victim lost consciousness after the assault.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Reviews Socio-Economic Development in Chatkal District
item.description: The President of Kyrgyzstan visited the Chatkal district in Jalal-Abad region to review its socio-economic development, implemented projects, and future plans. Investments totaling 20.6 billion soms were made between 2021 and September 2026. Tax revenue targets were met, and healthcare and education indicators improved.

item.title: Elon Musk Accuses Ukraine of Using Starlink for Attacks Aimed at Killing People
item.description: Elon Musk accused Ukraine's armed forces of using Starlink for offensive attacks intended to kill people, stating the loophole was closed last week. He confirmed SpaceX had limited Starlink's speed in Ukraine, emphasizing its crucial role in Ukraine's defense while criticizing 'hypocritical war-mongers'.

item.title: Protesters and Police Clash in Brussels During Anti-Government Demonstration
item.description: Belgian police used tear gas and pepper spray against protesters in Brussels who chanted anti-government slogans and demanded improvements to the education system. Clashes occurred after hundreds gathered for ongoing demonstrations. Police stated that measures were taken to ensure public order and safety.

item.title: Tariffs Could Help End Five Wars, Assesses Trump on Potential 200% Duties on Russian and Ukrainian Goods
item.description: US President Donald Trump suggested that tariffs could help end five wars. He evaluated the possibility of imposing 200% duties on goods from Russia and Ukraine.

item.title: President Japarov Comments on Alexey Shirshov's Role and State Asset Recovery
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov addressed the role of Alexey Shirshov, stating that politicians use Shirshov's name for criticism. He confirmed Shirshov's past involvement in energy system management and alleged corruption, detailing how information provided by Shirshov helped recover state assets worth approximately $20 million.

item.title: Direct Air Service Launched Between Astana and Oman
item.description: Air Astana has operated its inaugural flight on the Astana-Salalah route. The flight carried 140 passengers to Oman. Flights will be operated by Airbus A320 aircraft. This new route aims to develop tourism, trade, economic, and cultural ties between Kazakhstan and Oman.

item.title: Nurlan Orazalin Recounts Heated Debate During Adoption of Sovereignty Declaration
item.description: Nurlan Orazalin, a deputy of the 12th convocation of the Supreme Council of the Kazakh SSR, described the adoption of the Declaration of State Sovereignty as a complex and crucial period. He recalled a heated debate lasting seven hours, with 18 deputies voting against it.

item.title: Trump Considers Military Strike on Iran or a Diplomatic Deal
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated that a military strike on Iran could occur soon, but an agreement with Tehran also remains a possibility. He indicated the US was weighing the option of an attack while a major deal was also on the table. Trump expressed confidence in his handling of Iran, suggesting he might "finish the job" or Iran could agree to a deal, asserting the US would "win either way."

item.title: New 265-Bed Oncology Center to Be Built in Tashkent
item.description: A new 265-bed oncology center will be constructed in Tashkent as part of a medical cluster being established in collaboration with the Korean Eximbank. A contract for consulting services has been signed with a South Korean company for the project. The center will be built within the medical cluster.

item.title: Obama: We Prevented Iran from Obtaining Nuclear Weapons Through Diplomacy
item.description: Former US President Barack Obama stated that his administration prevented Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons through diplomatic means, without resorting to military action. He emphasized the success of diplomacy in achieving this objective, highlighting that no missiles were fired.

item.title: Iran Proposes Easing Export Barriers to Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Iraq
item.description: Iran is considering measures to remove obstacles for exporters trading with Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Iraq, according to a senior Foreign Ministry official. The proposals aim to address transportation and logistics challenges faced by Iranian exporters. These measures, approved by relevant government agencies, could facilitate regional trade.

item.title: France Sees Renewed Protests Against Rising Cost of Living
item.description: Mass protests against the rising cost of living have resumed in France, with over 800,000 people participating nationwide. Clashes between police and demonstrators occurred in Paris, where authorities used water cannons and tear gas. Similar incidents were reported in other major cities. Organizers claim 800,000 participated, while authorities estimate 410,000.

item.title: Global Wheat Prices Drop 12% in One Month Amid Improved Harvest Outlook
item.description: Global wheat prices have fallen by approximately 12% over the past month, reaching $229 per ton on the US exchange. Experts attribute the decline to improved harvest expectations for the current season. Major exporters like Russia and Ukraine are increasing shipments, influencing both global and domestic prices.
